fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Freelancer OAuth access token sent as the freelancer-oauth-v1 header: a Personal Access Token from https://accounts.freelancer.com/settings/develop ('valid for thirty days') or a token from your registered OAuth app.

adapter.rate_note: 'Each endpoint has a rate limit … A HTTP 429 response will be triggered if you hit the rate limit' (https://developers.freelancer.com/docs/api-overview/rate-limiting); no numbers are published. One request per second.
adapter.terms: Freelancer.com User Agreement forbids automated access to the API without express written permission; the OAuth app / personal token is that channel. The developer docs list 'Automatic Bidders' as a prohibited integration.

search.note: GET /projects/0.1/projects/active/ ('Searches for active projects', scope basic): query is space-separated terms over names and descriptions; limit/offset page the results; full_description=true returns the whole text. Freelancer projects are contracts, not employment: salary_min/max are budget.minimum/maximum in currency.code (fixed or hourly per `type`). time_submitted (Unix), owner_id, seo_url and jobs stay in raw. No location text filter (latitude/longitude only).

list_messages.note: GET /messages/0.1/messages/ (scope fln:messaging) filtered by threads[]=thread_id. The sender (from_user) is a numeric user id and time_created is Unix time; both stay in raw.

not_offered.me: Served by the Freelancer deals server (GET /users/0.1/self/); the jobs vocabulary keeps this entry to project discovery.
not_offered.apply: A Freelancer 'application' is a bid (POST /projects/0.1/bids/) that needs amount, period and milestone_percentage, which the jobs apply input (cover_letter, resume_url) does not carry — use the freelancer deals server's submit_bid.

evidence: host www.freelancer.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (GlobalSign nv-sa)
probe: 3/3 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 3/3 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
live read without credentials: get_posting, search returned data that validates against the vocabulary
